framing_preimages.name: node over leaves 0 and 1
framing_preimages.note: Also the root at leaf_count 2 and the height-1 peak at leaf_count 3. Pins the left and right argument order.

negative.name: left_to_right_fold
negative.reason: Produced by acc = leftmost peak then acc = MmrNodeV1(domain, acc, peak) over the remaining peaks left to right. The contract fixes the direction to right to left, so this value must be rejected.

negative.name: leaf_index_omitted
negative.reason: Produced by leaving u64_be(index) out of the leaf preimage. Order and repetition are then no longer locked by the tree, so this value must be rejected.

notes: MmrLeafV1(domain, index, leaf) = SHA256(ascii("TRUEOPEN_MMR_LEAF_V1") || u32_be(len(domain)) || domain || u64_be(index) || u64_be(len(leaf)) || leaf). The domain length is u32_be and the leaf length u64_be; the two widths differ on purpose.

MmrNodeV1(domain, left, right) = SHA256(ascii("TRUEOPEN_MMR_NODE_V1") || u32_be(len(domain)) || domain || left || right). MmrEmptyV1(domain) = SHA256(ascii("TRUEOPEN_MMR_EMPTY_V1") || u32_be(len(domain)) || domain).
Leaves are variable-length bytes, not Hash32, and index enters the leaf preimage, so the same bytes at a different position are a different leaf. The primitive never sorts, deduplicates or pads.

The peak list is determined by leaf_count alone: one peak per set bit of its binary form, highest on the left. peaks[] below is left to right, so an implementation can compare shape before it compares the root.
Folding is right to left: acc = rightmost peak, then acc = MmrNodeV1(domain, peak, acc) over the remaining peaks from right to left. leaf_count 1 roots to the leaf itself with no extra node layer.
leaf_count 0 roots to MmrEmptyV1(domain), never 32 zero bytes. A business protocol may exclude the empty list from its legal values, but it must not redefine this root.

root_hex at leaf_count 2 equals the height-1 peak at leaf_count 3: the minimal case of this contract rule 6, where the peaks of a k-leaf prefix are still nodes of the final tree. root_hex at leaf_count 3 is not in the 7-leaf tree, which is why a prefix proof verifies the peaks and recomputes the prefix root instead of searching for it.

negative left_to_right_fold is the only case that separates the two fold directions: leaf counts 1 through 6 agree byte for byte and 7 is the first that does not. An implementation that folds the other way passes every positive vector above, then diverges at any leaf count whose popcount is 3 or more.
source: Shared MMR_ROOT_V1 framing and the InferReceiptV3 output commitment.
